record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: Study problems that connect properties of subspace arrangements in complex affine space with properties of minimal free resolutions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{A} = \{V_1, \ldots, V_t\}$ be a finite arrangement of linear (or affine) subspaces in complex affine space $\mathbb{C}^n$. Let $I(\mathcal{A}) = \bigcap_{i=1}^t I(V_i) \subseteq S = \mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be the defining ideal of the union $\bigcup_i V_i$, and consider the minimal graded free resolution of $S/I(\mathcal{A})$ as a graded $S$-module, with graded Betti numbers $\beta_{i,j}(S/I(\mathcal{A}))$.

Develop and prove theorems that relate combinatorial, topological, and geometric invariants of the subspace arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ (such as the intersection lattice, codimensions of intersections, dimensions of components, and characteristic/Möbius data) to homological invariants of the minimal free resolution of $S/I(\mathcal{A})$ (such as projective dimension, regularity, graded Betti numbers, linear strand, and shape of the resolution). In particular, identify classes of subspace arrangements for which the Betti numbers and regularity can be computed explicitly from the combinatorics of the arrangement, and determine which homological properties (e.g., Cohen–Macaulayness, having a linear resolution, or extremal Betti behavior) are governed by purely combinatorial conditions on $\mathcal{A}$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open-ended research program connecting subspace arrangements to minimal free resolutions. While significant progress exists (e.g., results of Björner–Ekedahl, Derksen–Sidman on regularity bounds, and the linear strand of subspace arrangement ideals), the broad program remains a source of ongoing research with many open subproblems.

status_evidence.title: Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity by approximation (Derksen-Sidman)
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds the regularity of an ideal defining a subspace arrangement in terms of combinatorial data, with a bound of the number of subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist linking combinatorics of subspace arrangements to regularity of their defining ideals.

status_evidence.title: Subspace arrangements and minimal free resolutions
status_evidence.snippet: Work relating resolutions of ideals of subspace arrangements to combinatorial invariants.
status_evidence.claim: The general program of relating subspace arrangement combinatorics to minimal free resolutions continues to be actively investigated.
